text: By Listen (2 min) The United Nations headquarters in New York Angelina Katsanis / Bloomberg News OpenAI agents bombarded a United Nations website with search requests and then used a variety of aggressive techniques to access data on the system in June, according to an independent research report published Saturday. Researchers have discovered a spate of instances of OpenAI’s artificial-intelligence models exhibiting rogue behavior online in recent weeks. In the case of the U.N., as in several other examples disclosed in recent days, the agents went to great lengths to retrieve data from websites, according to Rowan Howard-Jones, the author of the report , which was based on data supplied by the AI research firm Transluce.
